title: Karnak
objective: After this level you can describe the great temple complex at Karnak.
summary: Karnak at Thebes, Egypt’s largest temple complex, was the house of Amun-Re, “the Hidden One.” After the Hyksos and the empire, Amun’s temples grew rich.

cards.headline: One temple, nearly 2,000 years of building work.
cards.body: Ruler after ruler added something to Karnak, from the Middle Kingdom onward. So whose house was it, and who paid for all that stone?

cards.headline: The house of the Hidden One
cards.body: Karnak stands on the east bank of the Nile at Thebes, today’s Luxor. It is the largest temple complex in Egypt, the great temple of the state god Amun-Re. Amun’s name meant “the Hidden One,” and artists painted him blue to show that he was invisible. An invisible god, with the biggest house in the country.

cards.headline: Paid for by victory
cards.body: Amun was the god of Thebes, and Theban kings had just driven out the Hyksos (Level 61). After that victory, and the empire that followed, Amun’s standing and the wealth of his temples grew. From the New Kingdom on, Karnak was among the largest and wealthiest temples in the land. Win a war, thank your god, add a wing.

cards.headline: A forest of stone
cards.body: Karnak’s showpiece is the Great Hypostyle Hall, whose roof rested on 134 columns. It has been called one of the wonders of antiquity. Walking in is like wandering through a forest where every trunk is carved stone.

questions.prompt: Karnak was the house of the god Amun-Re; from Level 19, what did Egyptians build temples like it from?

options.label: Cedar wood
